Synopsis:
Australia's remote Beetaloo shale gas basin (NT) is gaining strategic momentum amid the Iran conflict (started Feb 28), which has disrupted Qatari LNG flows through the Strait of Hormuz, spiking spot LNG prices to $25.80/MMBtu (+150%). With 200 tcf recoverable reserves and major players (Inpex, Santos) entering alongside smaller operators (Tamboran, Beetaloo Energy), Beetaloo is positioned as a geopolitically safe, proximate LNG supplier to Asia. Key bottleneck remains infrastructure build-out to Darwin or Queensland. Asian gas demand projected +30% over 10 years amplifies the strategic opportunity.
